text:
God made the world; with his divine voice

he drew it from chaos,

and, admiring his wondrous work,

they say he loved it.


His grand desire had been fulfilled,

magnificent, immortal;

but still, as a lover, he had yet to pour out

his heavenly affection.


And before the sweet gaze of his tenderness

the sphere fell into ecstasy,

and the angel of light and beauty

was changed into the moon.


And the pleasing fragrance of his noble breath

he cast over April,

and the angel of perfume in that instant

became the rose of the garden.


And from his gracious lips he breathed

the angel of honey;

the sweet, faithful bee became an emblem

of its delicate nectar.


And from his voice he formed sympathy,

a seductive echo,

and the angel of placid harmony

was changed into a nightingale.


Yet powerful God desired

to form a new being;

and he mercifully brought an angel from his Eden

and you were that woman.


And he adorned you with a diadem of beauty,

raised you like a deity;

gave your eyes a thousand pearls of tenderness,

of joy and pity.


And as an emblem, O Celia, of divine love,

the Maker wished to consecrate you

to the beneficent destiny

of the angel of love.

translation.title: The Angel of Love
translation.editorial_note: This text duplicates the preceding source poem apart from a minor accent difference; its translation is kept identical while retaining the supplied title.
